name: learned-masked-sparse-unet-detect-sot2993
description: SOT-2993 candidate (NOT promoted; champion byte-frozen, default-off hedge preserved). Self-trained 3D U-Net detector (temporal_unet3d) whose detection stage REPLACES the classical DoG+NMS, trained with MASKED SPARSE supervision: the loss is computed only inside a bounded anisotropic ellipsoid (radius_zyx=[4,12,12] voxels = 4*sigma) around each sparse GT annotation and is EXACTLY ZERO everywhere else (biohub_tracking.learned_detect.masked_sparse_loss_weights), so an unannotated real cell contributes no gradient and is never taught as background. This is the new-grounds cure for the sparse-GT Positive-Unlabeled contamination that made the earlier learned detectors fail (SOT-2828 numpy scorer / SOT-2848 naive-MSE degenerate 0.0 / SOT-2863 nnPU 0.1173 + Cellsparse soft-downweight 0.2753). The linking stage is the champion linker unchanged, so the leak-free CV A/B (experiments/sot2993/run_ab.py) isolates the detector. Weights are per-LOFO-fold artifacts (experiments/sot2993/weights/masked/<family>.pt), attachable offline as a Kaggle Dataset at /kaggle/input/biohub-claude-weights-sot2993/detector.pt (SOT-2847 offline attach->load->forward verdict FEASIBLE); no Kaggle submission from this child. See docs/ai/sot-2993-masked-sparse-unet-detector.md for the same-seed A/B evidence and promotion decision.
